clap is part of 6 of my public repositories, from 2016 to 2021.

What it was for: [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (4) and [Science and visualisation](@/projects/science.md) (2).

Most recently: [maze-rs](@/work/maze-rs.md): Maze generation algorithms from the book, in Rust; [streamflow](@/work/streamflow.md): Stream Flow - Fast Stream Processing in Rust; [sli2dli](@/work/sli2dli.md): SLI to DLI implementation written in rust. Nothing more, nothing less.

1 of these projects runs as a live site.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses clap: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links clap to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
